title: Two acids, same amount. Same pH?
hook: Two bottles hold the same amount of acid per litre. Will both be equally acidic?

knows: that acids are sour and can sting
that vinegar is a mild acid
that a lower pH means more acidic
doesNotKnow: that acidity comes from H⁺ released by acid molecules
that a weak acid releases H⁺ from only a small share of its molecules
that each pH step is a factor of 10 in free H⁺

misconception: The same concentration of any acid gives the same pH.
objective: The learner can explain that at 0.10 mol/L hydrochloric acid gives up all its H⁺ (pH 1.0) while acetic acid gives up H⁺ from only about 1 molecule in 75, so its pH is about 2.9: strength is the share that lets go, not the amount.

claims.text: Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid: in dilute water essentially every molecule gives up its H⁺, so 0.10 mol/L HCl has pH about 1.0.
claims.source: HCl fully dissociated in dilute aqueous solution (Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, ch. on acids and bases); pH = −log10(0.10) = 1.0. Activity effects make the measured pH about 1.1; the lesson says 'about'.

claims.text: Acetic acid, the acid in vinegar, is weak: at 0.10 mol/L only about 1 molecule in 75 gives up its H⁺, so its pH is about 2.9.
claims.source: Ka = 1.8e-5 at 25 °C (CRC Handbook, 'Dissociation constants of organic acids': 1.75e-5, pKa 4.756). Exact quadratic x = (−Ka + sqrt(Ka² + 4 Ka c)) / 2 = 1.333e-3 mol/L; pH 2.875; fraction 1.33% = 1 in 75 (node; Demo.tsx X_ACETIC). With Ka 1.75e-5: pH 2.88, 1 in 76.

claims.text: pH measures free H⁺: pH 1 is 0.1 mol/L of free H⁺, and each step up in pH means 10 times fewer.
claims.source: pH = −log10 of the hydrogen ion concentration in mol/L (IUPAC Gold Book, 'pH', simplified from activity).

claims.text: An acid's strength is the share of its molecules that give up H⁺, not how much acid there is.
claims.source: Strong vs weak acids defined by extent of dissociation (Ka); Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles.

claims.text: The stage is a toy: 75 drawn molecules stand for 0.10 mol/L in each beaker.
claims.source: Demo.tsx N = 75 so that the acetic fraction (1.33%) is exactly one drawn molecule; the stage shows 'of 75'.

recall.question: Lemon juice and a drain cleaner acid are made up to the same concentration. One has a much lower pH. That tells you it…
options: releases H⁺ from a larger share of its molecules
has more acid molecules per litre
recall.why: At equal concentration, the pH difference comes from strength: how many of the molecules let go of their H⁺.
